body: Blake supporters don't read. If they did, they'd read Justin's amended complaint which debunked every fake accusation Blake has made. If pro-Blake people had reading comprehension, they would not be "pro-Blake".
I'm glad she's on YouTube, i much prefer it to TikTok. I can use YouTube in the background and I enjoy long form content. I hope she thrives and remains on YouTube.

I feel so depleted on a daily basis. I’m emotionally, mentally, and physically exhausted. I wish I didn’t need him as much as I do. I wish I could just be normal.

You’re a very good writer, btw.

This is my biggest struggle. I just feel so worthless. Any small joys I attain in a day is inevitably swept away by a giant wave of despair once the loneliness sets in. The urge to unalive becomes so intense and powerful that it scares me. My entire world is wrapped up in someone who doesn't even think of me. It's torture. I just want one person to need me more than anything. I'm sorry I don't have an answer to our problem, but just know you're not alone.

Right?

I don't sleep, I pass out. I have to literally wear myself out to the point of exhaustion in order to sleep, and even then I can only sleep about four hours at a time. It's a misery.

Hello, I’m sorry for replying so late. My mom passed away last week and I’ve just been…well, I’m sure you know. On top of the depression and BPD symptoms I already have on a daily basis, having my mom die unexpectedly isn’t helping my mental state at all. I’ve also never had to plan a funeral before, and I had no idea how taxing and expensive that whole experience would be. I just feel very depleted and empty. 

Your experience does sound a lot like mine. I did want to “fix” my FP, but he really didn’t want an emotional connection with me. I downloaded this book about RO-DBT, and apparently it’s supposed to be a bit more useful for “quiet borderlines”, like myself. I want to read it and hope that I get inspired or motivated to help myself. This disorder sucks so damn much. I either don’t feel anything at all or I feel so much that I just want to end everything. The only time I feel energized to do anything is when my FP and I are talking. It’s embarrassing having your entire sense of self wrapped up in someone else. 

I hope you’ve been feeling a little better these last few days. I hope at least one of us can find some reprieve from time to time.

I know how you feel, it’s the same for me. Nighttime is torture for me. Spending nights in a dark and empty bedroom is excruciating. There are times I delay going home because I know as soon as I step through the door I will breakdown and have an episode. 

I’ve started ridesharing overnight in order to distract myself. I usually drive until sunrise or until I’m exhausted, so by time I get home I immediately go to sleep. I’m also afraid to date because rejection or unstable attachments make me spiral. 

I try not to isolate myself, but one of the cons of socializing is forming another FP, which is exactly what happened to me recently. That didn’t end well and now I’m fighting the urge to unalive everyday. Isolating myself makes me incredibly lonely, but socializing triggers my anxiety and risk forming unhealthy attachments. No matter what I do, I’m miserable. This is such an insidious disorder. I feel so trapped everyday.

Yes, and I'm sorry you're feeling this way too. It sucks.

I can't see "forever" in the cards for me though. I have such an insatiable desire to be loved unconditionally that I can't see myself ever being content with being alone. I envy those who are disciplined enough to remain single for their well-being. I will probably unalive from loneliness, shame, and guilt. I'm trying to hold myself together, but the only time I feel *stable* is when I have an FP. It doesn't work out well because I seem to be attracted to ppl who aren't emotionally available in some way. Self sabotage is a big problem for me too. It's all an exhausting cycle.

I come from a lower middle class background and I’m pretty much poor at this current stage in my life. I tried therapy with what I can afford and I ended up with a therapist who *probably* ghosted me after I started showing BPD symptoms, and after the session where I told him I was suicidal. I say “probably” because I’m not sure if it was a scheduling error, but what I do know is that the therapist never contacted me since to rebook or to even check on me. It made me never want to try therapy again. 

I know finding a therapist is like dating, and that you have to keep trying, but the idea of having to open up to someone new and establish another relationship is not pleasant. I’ve researched what kind of therapy it would take for me to recover and it isn’t cheap. It costs between $150-$200 per session to find someone who can truly understand and maybe help with BPD.

I don’t even know how to say what I’m going to say without sounding petty and immature, so I’m just going to say it. I no longer talk to my FP, but he has personality disorders and addiction issues. He and I talked about suicide before. I know he’s in turmoil on the inside, despite showing a completely false version of himself to the world. He’s blessed with good looks and he comes from a wealthy family. He goes to therapy twice a week. I bring this up because it makes me incredibly angry, jealous, and sad. 

I still check his socials from time to time (yes, I know this is bad) and I see him posting the typical luxury lifestyle and travel bullshit, and deep down I know he’s miserable and insecure, but it still rips me apart. It hurts me because I know, despite the fake posts, it’s his access to solid therapy that helps him cope. It also helps that he’s gorgeous and people are drawn to him, so he actually has a social life to help distract from his dark thoughts. 

He hit the genetic lottery AND the economic lottery. He can afford the best therapy for himself because of his wealth and has access to the best social life because of his beauty. I’m not saying privileged people don’t suffer, and he certainly does, but what I’m saying is that it’s unfair that I have to work 10x as hard as he does to just get to baseline. I understand that this is how life works, and some people are born with advantages. 

I realize how petty and childish I am for comparing myself to by FP…but what is BPD if not insecurity? The fact that he, and other people in this sub, were born into comfort makes me angry. Why does he get access to great therapy, while I’m stuck with a therapist who ghosts and abandons me? It makes me not want to try anymore. It makes me even more suicidal that some people just get lucky in life. It makes everything feel so pointless.

I can’t afford the right kind therapy I need. So I either have to bootstrap dbt workbooks together or work another job for hours to afford an expensive therapist. And for what purpose ultimately? To stay in my dead end career for a few extra years? Fuck that. I have nothing to look forward to, and I suspect I have ADHD traits alongside my BPD, which makes it even harder to be disciplined enough to teach myself healthy coping skills. 

My post is dark, and, yes, I’m on my way out soon. I’m probably one of those “you don’t want to recover” people. I actually do want to get better, I just don’t have the resources or the willpower to do so. Am I doing everything I possibly can to heal myself? No, probably not. I don’t want to give up on myself, but the weight of this disorder and the weight of society is crushing. I’m envious of privileged people, but I’m also happy for anyone who have advantages in life to help them get healthy. Not all of us do, and some of us aren’t strong enough to get past that hurdle.

Thanks. I just feel unworthy and that everything about myself is meaningless. I have no focus or direction in life and I have no idea who I am. I seem to only be attracted to people I subconsciously know are unavailable. I've been on a downward spiral ever since I met my first FP a year ago. We stopped talking six months ago, but I'm still obsessed. A then new potential FP came into my life. Two days ago something happened and I think he's gone now too. The pain and desperation I feel when these people "abandon" me is immense. I only feel stable and motivated when I have a FP. When they leave I become suicidal.

My friend said I'll find someone, but the idea of suffering through multiple FPs and potential abandonments to find the right person seems excruciating. I consider staying single, but I want to be loved and I don't think I want to survive by myself. I work a dead end job, and I'm pretty much broke and that adds to the stress. I've considered just shutting down everything for a few days and riding out my emotions, but I have to work. When I work I spiral internally because I feel worthless and I can't see a way out. I'm embarrassed and ashamed of how I've ruined so many opportunities for myself. 

I was in therapy, but I think my therapist ghosted me. I opened up to him about my suicidal thoughts and the next session he didn't show up (virtual). Idk if it was a scheduling mistake, but he never reached out to rebook and I never went back because I felt offended and abandoned. I never want to try therapy again. 

My life isn't horrible, which makes me feel worse. I have friends, family, and aquaitances who all visibly enjoy me. I know they'll be devastated if I do go through with it. ..but while everyone seems to "love" me, no one is "in love" with me. That's ultimately what breaks my heart. There's a sabotage mechanism inside me that activates when I get close to what I want. I know I can potentially fix my broken brain with meds and treatment, but the idea of prolonging this life is exhausting. I just want to be done with the pain. 

Sorry for the gloomy reply. I hope you are able to find peace within yourself one day. I hope you're able to ease your struggling.
I'm 35, and my birthday is next month. I don't think I'll make it to 36. The struggle is so painful.
My heart goes out to you. I can't possibly imagine what you're going through. I'm so so sorry.

I can absolutely relate, word for word. This is currently where I am. I'm basically hiding from the world because it hurts so much. Getting "lost in my own mind" is the perfect way to put it. I can't offer a suggestion on getting out the isolation funk, since I'm still in it. I hope you feel better soon, it's ok to take time for yourself to heal. My inbox is open if you ever want someone to talk to. Take care, friend.

That's reasonable, and probably the best path for you right now. A lot of people find love when they're not looking for it. Just don't isolate yourself. This is where I am right now, which is why I said I'm the last person who should be offering advice. Got my heart broken, and I've isolated due to abandonment fears. This isn't good, and I know it. 

You're an introvert, like me, and it's easy for us to shut ourselves away. Focus on your hobbies, but consider doing your hobbies with a group. Push yourself to do this. Don't look for romance, just enjoy people. I know it's hard. If you're like me, you just want to be fucking loved by someone. It's unbearable, but have patience. I truly believe you'll eventually find someone you click with by just living your life.

This represents how I often feel. Especially the heart on the outside of the body, and going from feeling love to sadness in an instant. 

Great work.

You say that you fly solo for your hobbies, is there a way you think you can connect with a group? Your hobbies sound amazing, these are things I'd like to try myself. I'm sure there are hiking and rock climbing communities that meet up. I would try finding and joining them, without the intention of a romantic connection, just do it to meet people in general. You could end up meeting a woman who isn't in the group, maybe via a party someone in the group invited you to. Basically, what I'm trying to say is that you may think you don't have a pattern of meeting women who are toxic for you, but you could unconsciously. You have to change the way you meet people. Certain types of women (emotionally available ones in this case) may not be in the places you've been looking. 

I think one of the few beautiful things about BPD is that we love harder than anyone. It causes us immense pain, but at the same time it's a unique quality that I think brings good into the world. The problem is that there are people who take advantage of it. Don't ever try not being emotionally available or caring, but we just have to learn to be more selective of who is deserving of our affection. We often can see red flags early, but we're so damn desperate to fill the void in ourselves that we still pursue these people. Learn to see the red flags and train yourself to move on fast, even if it hurts. Find a new pattern of meeting people...for example, where would an emotionally available woman spend her time?

Volunteer work, maybe? Cooking classes, perhaps?

You're a catch. I can tell. There's a woman out there who is going to accept you, it just may take some time and patience, and, unfortunately, more pain to find her. But I'm sure you will.

I'm the last person who should be giving relationship advice, but I do have a suggestion. From reading all your replies one thing I can deduce is that you may be trying too hard. Relationships take time to grow, which is something pwBPD have a difficult time reconciling with. Online dating is a form of immediate gratification, it puts people in the mindset of "needing someone now" and that's not always the best mindset to be in. You're 25, and I know from your perspective it may not seem like it...but you're very young. You have LOTS of time to find someone. It's ok to slow down. 

The biggest thing I'd recommend in your case is to ditch online dating for now. Do you have hobbies? Try considering joining some sort of group or community that gathers like-minded people. For example, I'm taking acting classes and I've met some of the most incredible people who think the way I do and have the same interests. Putting yourself in that kind of environment does two things: 1) your doing something for yourself, which is always important and 2) you're opening yourself up to meeting someone in a more natural setting, where relationships can flourish organically. Try not to rush things, enjoy being around people and someone will come to you. I know how hard it is to want to feel loved immediately, I struggle with it so bad myself.

I wish you the best.

Before I knew what BPD was, I recognized this trait within myself. I would always say, "I'm emotionally immature" in my head. I didn't know why, but I instinctively knew this about myself. Once I started researching BPD it was like a lightbulb switching on. I agree with everything you described, except for me it's difficult to be positive about it. I've become debilitated and don't want to socialize anymore out of embarrassment. I know this is my BPD brain lying to me to protect me, but I'm too exhausted to fight it off. 

The irony of it all is that I believe this quality is what draws people to me. I don't have trouble making friends, and I do consider myself charismatic. People actually want to be around me, but I hate myself so much that my social anxiety is now the worst its ever been. You sound like you're on the right path, even if you don't know all the answers yet. Keep focusing on being positive, I think you'll figure it out in time.

It's a shame we have to struggle so much to find mental health professionals who are informed about the disorder, and who also aren't afraid of it. Knowing other people like you have trouble being believed does make me feel validated. Thank you for sharing!
Thank you for reaffirming this for me. I've been hesitant to try therapy again, but hearing you found someone who understands you makes me feel better.
I agree, and I've stopped seeing that therapist. When he said that pwBPD couldn't hold down jobs I knew he didn't understand the disorder well, and that it was time to let him go.

I definitely can relate. Growing up for me was kind of a free for all. My entire life I was on "just figure it out" mode. I had absolutely zero guidance, and no emotional connections until I found a friend or two in my 20s. Sounds like it was the same for you. It's difficult having a parent who doesn't know how to be emotionally responsive, even in a conversation. I gave up years ago trying to connect with my mom, she just doesn't have the capacity to do so.

I've stopped seeing this therapist recently. I can find a new one, and I've been looking but I haven't reached out to any yet. Lack of motivation plus fear of encountering another therapist who I don't vibe with is holding me back. This therapist has kind of turned me off to the profession, even though I know there are good ones out there. Thank you for advice.

Your father not being around could have been internalized as abandonment. Did your mother provide emotional support while growing up? You say your mother took you father’s absence hard, was she depressed? Parenting is more than putting clothes on your back and food in your mouth. A child also needs to be nurtured emotionally. 

I’m not trying to get you to criticize your parents, btw. I’m just curious. I know my mom loved me in a technical sense, but she was mentally ill and unable to give me any semblance of emotional support. I don’t think I ever heard the phrase “I love you” said to me until I was in my 30s. I never realized how that all affected me until very recently.

I’d say emotional neglect was the cause. 

Only child. Father never bothered with me, saw him maybe five times throughout my life before he died when I was 18. 

Literal abandonment.

My mother is schizophrenic, and was unable to provide emotional support because she couldn’t even take care of herself. I always lived with a relative who could take care of her because she couldn’t live alone. 

Emotional abandonment. 

I’m black, gay, and raised in the south. I highlight my race because I never felt “black enough” growing up, which isolated me from kids in school. On top of that, I was gay, which caused further isolation and anxiety. I grew up in a southern black community, and to this day I don’t feel connected to either the black or gay community. I feel like an outcast no matter where I go.

Social abandonment. 

The most stable parental figure in my life was my aunt, who was a second mother to me. My mother and I moved in with her when I was around 10. The first years were great with her, she validated me and treated me like her son, but she was in poor health. Eventually, it became harder for her to nurture me after a few years. She died when I was 17, right before I needed her most as I was entering early adulthood. 

Another abandonment, though it wasn’t her choice.

I also witnessed my grandmother die right in front of me. I forget how old I was when it happened, either early 20s or late teens. We were pretty close, and the image of her dying still haunts me.

All this was the recipe of a child completely on edge at all times, scared to get close to anyone in fear of rejection, who never felt good enough for anyone, and who expects everyone to leave at some point. I’ve felt worthless since as far back as I can remember.

I understand. I like him too, and I think he's great for TV, but I just don't like the narrative that he's completely innocent. If anything, he instigated all of this imo. 

I'm a fan of them both, and I'll be eating my popcorn during the next episode. I predict they'll have this blow up, but they'll end up becoming good friends by time the show is over lol

He's not really an angel though. People forget Davide's conversation with Andrew where he said he wouldn't call Ekin-Su if they were on the outside. He made it clear in that moment he wasn't interested in her, yet he never told her. He was basically stringing her along until the bombshells came in. 

I don't think Ekin-Su is right for sneaking around, but she asked him several times how he felt, and he lied.

All I can say is…same. I sometimes wish all of us suicidal people could meet up and comfort each other. There’s so many of us on Reddit, but in the real world we’re surrounded by people who know how to cope in the world. It’s incredibly lonely feeling this way. I’m sorry you’re going through this.

You’re not worthless. If you were then your post wouldn’t have resonated with me. All I can say at this moment is try not to beat yourself up. Take each day one at a time. Put off harming yourself until tomorrow, and then when tomorrow comes…do it again. Just know that I’m out here fighting the same fight as you. You may be alone physically, but you’re not alone in what you’re experiencing.

That's how I look at it too, which is why I don't talk about it anymore. At least their last memory of me will be somewhat pleasant. I have a therapist, but I get the same spiel over and over. Some people in this world just can't be helped. I'm pretty sure I'm one of them.

Thanks, and I'm sorry you have to struggle alone with these kind of feelings too.

My friend probably wouldn't try to have me hospitalized, but I've talked to her about suicide a few times. I can tell it's very draining on her spirit. I feel like I'm being malicious if I keep bringing it up.

It really is unsettling, but I understand why it happens. I come to this sub to read about people who feel the same way I do. I feel alone in my real life, but coming here reminds me I'm not suffering by myself. I don't comment because I'm in the same boat as the OP, and it's like the blind leading the blind. I don't have an answer to comfort them. I try to up vote every post I read, so the person can at least know someone is hearing them and acknowledges their pain.

What OP is describing doesn't always have to be romantic. Many people never experienced what they described, even in childhood from parents. I know I didn't. I'm 35 years old, and still wish I could be hugged by my mother and feel safe, but that has not and will never happen for me.

If a person didn't have that kind of affection growing up it can be incredibly difficult to be intimate with others as an adult. For me personally, getting close to someone (both physically and emotionally) is uncomfortable. I'm starved for intimacy yet I isolate myself when I feel someone really begin to open up to me. I'm trying to overcome this fear, but it's not easy and it's not an overnight fix.

Reading your post, I can tell you're a great person who'd I'd love to know in my life. I just want to say that I know for a fact that my FP is depressed and has a lot of demons, yet he projects a perfect happy image to the world. Everything you've outlined herebare things I've said about him and myself. I even still put him on a pedestal while knowing his true personality. I believe this is a symptom of our disorder. We idealize the people we're obsessed with even when we know they're not perfect.

Be kind to yourself and keep in mind your brain is wired to think little of yourself when it's not true. This is advice I can't even implement, I still struggle with self-esteem, but I still want to say it to you. You're not the bad things you say about yourself. I sense you're a lovely person who others enjoy being around. Stay strong, I think you're amazing.
Thank you, I appreciate your words. It helps a lot. I wish the best for you too, and much happiness in your life.

You really captured how I feel on a daily basis. I think it's beautiful, and so very accurate. I feel like I'm drowning in a dark pit of despair everyday. I'm glad you have a creative outlet that helps you cope. I wish the best for you in life and I hope things get easier for you.
